commits.message:
zephyr version 0.0.4

    created initial (default) database initialization

zephyr version 0.0.3

    updated zephyr_db_schema.xml to reflect the current state of the
    zephyr_db_schema.sql, except for the 5-way composite foreign key in
    the request table

zephyr version 0.0.2

    created initial sqlite3-based database schema

zephyr version 0.0.1

    zephyr is service that provisions cloud-based computing resources to
    augment fixed-resource batch systems based on user job demand.

gpse version 0.6.6. include dNx, dNy, and dNz settings in standard
output.

gpse version 0.6.5. reorganized main time propagation/simulation loop
to allow wave function data to be reprocessed; i.e., allows users to
read in wave functions from a previous simulation and recompute
expectation values, probability currents, average velocities, etc.;
continued moving source code to pep-8-like format

gpse version 0.6.4. implemented and verified computation of average
velocities across same boundaries where the probability currents are
computed in pmca module; also verified results for probability currents
and velocities using ansatz wave function for simple harmonic oscillator
ring potential

gpse version 0.6.3. implemented computation of probability currents
along z-axis in x-y plane for each Cartesian quadrant to provide
measurement of out-of-plane dynamics

gpse version 0.6.2. implemented and verified computation of several
probability currents about the z-axis of the system; currently, four
currents are computed, where each represent the probabiity current
passing from one Cartesian (volume) quadrant in the x-y plane to the
next about the z-axis; these numerically computed probability currents
were verified by comparing them against the analytically computed
currents for the wave function solution to a 3D axisymmetrical simple
harmonic oscillator potential

gpse version 0.6.1. implemented grid_linear_search function and
grid_nearest_point subroutine in grid module to support new
probability/mass current analysis module (pmca); the grid_nearest_point
subroutine will be utilized by the pmca module to help determine
integration limits over which the probability/mass currents and average
velocites of the wave function will be computed on different surfaces
within the three-dimensional, regular grid; continued reformatting
source code into a 72 character wide, pep8-like format

gpse version 0.6.0. implemented VTK reader function (io_read_vtk) to
support simple parallel I/O reads of input wave function; added logical
flag (chkptOn) to control whether or not checkpoint wave function is
written out at the end of each simulation; started reformatting source
code into a 72 character wide, pep8-like format

gpse version 0.5.9. initial wave functions computed by psi_init are now
also normalized numerically; this provides support for approximate
analytic wave functions where normalization constants are not known
analytically; also reverted to serialized binary checkpoint from v0.5.6

gpse version 0.5.3. added ability to write out integrated density
profiles of the wave functions in (x,y)-, (x,z)-, and (y,z)-planes.

gpse version 0.5.2. added ability to reduce grid point resolution
of wave functions in vtk-formatted output files from the full grid
point resolution of the simulation. intended usage is to reduce
output file size, when necessary.

gpse version 0.5.1. Reformatted source code to conform to a 132
character linewidth.
gpse version 0.5.0. Added more formal documentation to source code.

gpse version 0.4.9. modified the subroutine psi_boost in psi module
to include boundary points. if boundary points are not included,
then they will not be properly boosted with the interior points.
this issue did not previously exist when initial wavefunctions were
originally loaded into memory completely on the MPI_MASTER process
before being distributed to the other MPI processes.

gpse version 0.4.8. Added an analytical approximation of the
wavefunction solution to the Schrodinger equation for a single
particle in a simple harmonic oscillator ring potential. This
approximate wavefunction is only intended to be used as an initial
state guess to imaginary time propagation calculations. e.g., note
that the computed wavefunction is not normalized properly.

gpse version 0.4.7. Created rot module to build the basic rotation
matrices using array functions. Rotation matrices will be used to
perform time-dependent transformations on the angular velocity
vector of the rotating frame. Added two ad-hoc time-dependent
transformations: (1) nutation of the angular velocity vector about
the x-axis and (2) a tanh-based rotation of the angular velocity
vectory about the y-axis.

gpse version 0.4.6. Hard coded variable psiFilePos to be KIND = 8
integer as a temporary workaround for a 32-bit integer overflow
that occurs when attempting to write out wave functions to vtk
(and probably also bin) file formats using streaming I/O when the
number of grid points is large. e.g., when nX * nY * nZ >= 512^3.

gpse version 0.4.5. Modified the subroutines grk4_f_gp_3d_rrf_cd2
and grk4_f_gp_3d_rrf_cd4 to allow for users to specify the location
of the centre of rotation. Note: evua module subroutines do not yet
account for a centre of rotation away from the origin of the
Cartesian coordinate system specified on the computational grid.

gpse version 0.4.4. Reintroduced expectation values, uncertainties,
and other measured quantities with respect to the center of mass.

gpse version 0.4.3. Continued cleaning up main gpse program as well
as io module. Removed unused and deprecated subroutines.

gpse version 0.4.2. Cleaned up main gpse program as well as evua
module. Eliminated use of the full-reduce I/O subroutines from io
module to read and write wave functions to file. Only support the
partial-reduce I/O subroutines now, which will eliminate MPI_MASTER
memory bottleneck. Appended evua_ prefix to all remaining functions
and subroutines in evua module to continue standardizing source.

gpse version 0.4.1. Improved modularization of evua in order to
help simplify readability of main gpse program and source file.

gpse version 0.4.0. Added GRK4-related subroutines to update the
intermediate wave functions at each stage of the algorithm to the
grk4 module.

gpse version 0.3.9. Began migrating GRK4-related functions and
subroutines back into a grk4 module to help better organize the
main gpse source file gpse.f90.

gpse version 0.3.8. Fixed up a working, but ugly attempt at writing
formatted vtk files with using streaming I/O. See psiOutput == -4.

gpse version 0.3.7. Added several unsuccessful attempts to extend
new stream I/O functionality to formatted vtk files.

gpse version 0.3.6. Added stream I/O functionality for reading in
and writing out wave functions and/or external potentials from
unformatted binary files. This will enable gpse to reduced memory
usage on MPI_MASTER from its current polling I/O mode. i.e., it
will eliminate the need for Vex3f and Psi3f to perform full I/O.
gpse version 0.3.5. Completed and tested new input subroutines.

gpse version 0.3.4. Rewrote how gpse handles io. Only completed
and tested output portion so far.

gpse version 0.3.3. Added io module subroutine to support the
ability to read input wave functions, external potentials and
RECTILINEAR_GRID point configurations from legacy VTK files.

gpse version 0.3.2. OpenMP clauses rewritten to utilize PARALLEL
DOs and the IF clause to enable loop parallelization over the y-dim
of the system when there is only one active ( i.e., non-ghost )
z-point/xy-slice per MPI process. This should allow for greater
scalability at high processor/core counts.

gpse version 0.3.1. Added rotation terms to calculations of both
energy expectation value and chemical potential.

gpse version 0.3.0. Removed dependencies on ISO_FORTRAN_ENV module
KIND type parameters. Replaced these dependencies with custom KIND
type parameters in math module.

gpse version 0.2.9. Removed temporary functions and subroutines
used to double check Sagnac effect simulation results. Removed
lib_vtk_io module source files from tracking. Removed old input
files from tracking. Added consolidated input file gpse.input to
tracking.

gpse version 0.2.8. Consolidated namelist input into one single file
in order to simplify input/job submission process on clusters. Also
added some temporary functions and subroutines that will be used to
check Sagnac effect simulations.

gpse version 0.2.7. Modified main program subroutines as well as
io module subroutines to use three-dimensional arrays for writing
wave functions and external potentials to file. Previously,
one-dimensional arrays were used to conform with lib_vtk_io's
formatting requirements. Also began rewriting main program's
functions and subroutines to use more explicit argument lists as
has already been done with evua module's functions and subroutines.

gpse version 0.2.6. Standard output bug found. When standard output
is piped out to a file and fullIO = .TRUE., standard output stops
writing to file after awhile and begins writing to the file fort.6
instead. Bug doesn't appear to occur if fullIO = .FALSE. See GCC's
Bugzilla description of Bug 50926. Bug did not occur when write_vtk
used the lib_vtk_io module.

gpse version 0.2.5. Added custom write_vtk subroutine to io module.
This custom subroutine will be used to eliminate gpse's dependence
on the lib_vtk_io module, which often has issues with older fortran
compilers. All lib_vtk_io module dependencies have been commented
out for the time being.

gpse version 0.2.4. Modified all expectation value functions in
the evua module to allow them to be computed with respect to a
specific reference point and/or axis. e.g., gpse's basic output
now includes the calculation of the expectation values with respect
to both the origin of the computational grid as well as the center
of mass of the condensate. This will be helpful in decoupling center
of mass motion from other dynamics. Also began rewriting all functions
and subroutines to use explicit argument lists as opposed to
relying on implicitly accessible module variables. These explicit
argument lists will decrease the dependency between modules.

gpse version 0.2.3. Implemented boost operator. Boost operator is
applied to initial wave function to allow user to impart an initial
velocity to the condensate.

gpse version 0.2.2. Added functions to compute the squared
angular momentum expectation values using 4th-order central
differences. Also added functions to compute the force and torque
expectation. Both 2nd- and 4th-order central difference versions
were implemented. Added functions to compute the moments of inertia
with respect to user-defined axes. Currently, the moments are
computed with respect to the axes passing through the center of
mass and the grid origin.

gpse version 0.2.1. Imaginary time propagation fully supported.
When full IO is enabled, the last wave function written to a
formatted output file is now also checkpointed in a binary
(unformatted) output file. This binary may be read back into gpse
to restart a simulation that terminated prematurely or, if the
simulation was running in imaginary time, then it may be used as
the ITP-converged initial wave function of the real, forward time
simulation. Also began adding support for a gnuplot-style file
format (.gpi).

gpse version 0.2.0. Rolled back floating-point optimizations. Added
mpi_gather_custom subroutine to collect external potential and
wave function data from all MPI processes onto MPI_MASTER. Enabled
ability to write external potential and wave function data to .vtk
file from MPI_MASTER.

gpse version 0.1.9. Optimized floating-point operations in the
main program subroutines f_gp_3d_rrf_cd2 and f_gp_3d_rrf_cd4 as
well as the main GRK4 steps/updates. Speedup testing only shows
minor improvement over 'unoptimized' floating-point versions.

gpse version 0.1.8. Improved modularization. Moved a majority of
main program variables to modules. Added module-specific input
files. Added housekeeping subroutines to modules. e.g., read
module-specific input files, write module-specific input parameters
to file, broadcast module-specific input parameters to all MPI
processes, etc. Successfully tested classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta
scheme with 2nd-order central differences for strong nonlinear
atom-atom interactions in a rotating reference frame.

gpse version 0.1.7. Removed grk4 module. grk4 module subroutines
moved to main program CONTAINS statement ( see gpse.f90 ). Fixed a
bug in the subroutine f_gp_3d_rrf_cd2 -- an extra minus sign in the
diagonal elements of the matrix was observed to break conservation
of mass and energy during test simulations. Added the subroutines
f_gp_3d_rrf_cd6 and f_gp_3d_rrf_cd8, which compute the
vector-valued function f ( t , y ) in the GRK4 method defined for
the GPE and use 6th- and 8th-order central differences,
respectively, to approximate its differential terms. Neither of
these subroutines have been tested yet. Added pgf90 compiler
options to Makefile.

gpse version 0.1.6. First working development version of the gpse
codebase that provides a limited functionality for solving the
time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equation ( GPE ) in a rotating
reference frame using the Generalized 4th-Order Runge-Kutta
( GRK4 ) Method of Lines approach with finite differences. Added
grk4 module, which at present only contains the subroutines that
compute the vector-valued function f ( t , y ) defined for the GPE
using 2nd- and 4th-order central differences. GRK4 stages,
intermediate wave functions, MPI communication patterns for
workload / boundary condition distribution, and expectation value
and uncertainty calculations are currently all handled in main
program's time loop. Tested the forward time propagated solution of
the linear Schrodinger equation ( gS = 0 ) in an inertial frame
( wX = wY = wZ = 0 ) for each lambda-variant of GRK4+CD4 over a few
oscillator units of time with an initial Gaussian ground state and
single vortex state ( mL = 1 ). Norm, energy, and angular momentum
were all conserved. All other expectation and uncertainty values
showed expected behavior / values. Limited testing of GRK4+CD2 when
lambda = 2 was also performed. All tests performed with MPI only;
i.e. OpenMP was disabled.

gpse version 0.1.5. Added large number of evua module functions to
compute common expectation values. Both 2nd- and 4th-order central
difference operator implementations provided for most functions.
All functions written to assume they will be called from an MPI
process. Outer control loops within each function parallelized
with OpenMP. Tested functions by checking computed expectation
values against theoretically predicited expectation values for
wave functions currently available in psi module. These initial
tests were successful (after a few bug fixes here and there).

gpse version 0.1.4. Converted all Vex1, Vex2, Vex3 and Vex4 arrays
to REALs from COMPLEXs. The ability to handle complex external
potentials will be added in a future version of gpse.

gpse version 0.1.3. Converted all psi and vex module functions to
subroutines in order to offload more work from main program source
to modules. Most !$OMP compiler directives now contained within
these new module subroutines. Explicitly defined upper and lower
bounds of arrays passed to these subroutines in order to avoid
out-of-bound index errors that may occur when called due to use of
non-standard index bounds to accommodate MPI parallelization. Began
adding functions to evua module to calculate expectations values.

gpse version 0.1.2. Added wave function and external potential
initialization before main time propagation loop. When initial
wave function and external potential are not read in from file,
they are computed across all MPI processes using functions
defined in the psi and vex modules. Each MPI process is in turn
parallelized internally across a number of OpenMP threads set
using the OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable. Also added basic
outline of main time propagation loop and variables declarations
for expectation value and uncertainty relation analysis.

gpse version 0.1.1. Setup input parameter file ( gpse.in ) to be
read in from MPI_MASTER process using NAMELIST I/O statements. All
input parameters are then MPI_BCAST to all MPI processes from the
MPI_MASTER process. Also added status-related messeages that are
written to standard output to provide user with updates on general
program information and progress when run.

gpse version 0.1.0. Updated grid module's regular_grid_axis
subroutine to provide support for defining sub-grid boundary points
across MPI processes. Added data type checking to determine both
the default and machine/compiler-specific KIND precision(s) that
are supported. Precision of MPI elementary data types to be used
are then set based on these KIND(s).

gpse version 0.0.9. Added lib_vtk_io, lib_base64 and ir_precision
modules from LIB_VTK_IO v1.1 written by Stefano Zaghi. LIB_VTK_IO
is implemented as a submodule of gpse's io module to provide VTK
(Visualization Tookit) formatted output files of external potential
and wave function data for visualization with the open source,
parallel visualization and graphical analysis tools Paraview and
VisIt, both of which support the VTK framework and format. Tested
LIB_VTK_IO's write support for legacy VTK format with data on a
RECTILINEAR_GRID. Paraview VTK reader had a problem importing data
written in single precision, but imported data written in double
precision successfully. VTK's XML format(s) not tested yet. VisIt
VTK reader not tested yet.

gpse version 0.0.8. main gpse.f90 file added. also added evua and
io modules. evua module will contain all functions, subroutines,
parameters, variables and arrays for calculating a wide range of
expectation values and uncertainty relations to help analyze the
results produced by the gpse simulations. io module will contain
all input/output-related functions, subroutines, parameters,
variables and arrays for gpse. started setting up for opemmp and
mpi.

gpse version 0.0.7. vex module added. vex module contains all
functions, subroutines, parameters, variables and arrays for
generating a variety of external potentials to act on the particle
and/or condensate in gpse simulations.

gpse version 0.0.6. psi module added. psi module contains all
functions, subroutines, parameters, variables and arrays for
generating wavefunctions to serve as initial conditions for gpse
simulations.

gpse version 0.0.5. grid module added. grid module will handle all
functions, subroutines and variables used to define computational
grid(s) on which gpse will model the condensate wavefuctions,
external potentials, and so on.

gpse version 0.0.4. hermite function added to math module. hermite
passed initial functional testing.

gpse version 0.0.3. laguerre and associated laguerre functions
added to math module. both laguerre and alaguerre passed initial
functional testing.

gpse version 0.0.2. git now tracking Makefile. factorial function
added to math module. factorial passed initial functional testing.

gpse version 0.0.1. gpse rebuild begins again with git tracking
all changes and modifications. math module to provide mathematical
constants and functions to support other gpse modules.

condor_annex version 0.0.6

Changed EC2InstanceID in EE-ec2-startd-attrs to $(EC2InstanceID). This
resolves the "CONFIGURATION PROBLEM: Failed to insert ClassAd attribute
EC2InstanceID = i-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. The most common reason for this is
that you forgot to quote a string value in the list of attributes being
added to the STARTD ad."

condor_annex version 0.0.5

Removed the s3:deleteObject action on the S3PoolPassword and
S3ConfigFile in the lambda_cleanup_policy found in
CloudFormation/template-2. This prevents deletion of the pool password
and user configuration files stored in a static S3 bucket when the
--password-url and --config-url command-line options are used. Note,
however, this may lead the deletion of the S3DeleteBucket to fail when
the --password-file and --config-file options are used instead. i.e.,
the S3 bucket dynamically created with the --password-file and
--config-file options will no longer be non-empty when the annex's
CloudFormation stack attempts to clean itself up and shutdown.

condor_annex version 0.0.4

The "Runtime" : "nodejs" parameter is no longer supported for creating
and/or updating AWS Lambda functions. If condor_annex is executed with
this deprecated runtime, the ActivateAlarm, CleanUp, and Plumbing Lambda
functions are not created, causing the annex's CloudFormation Stack to
rollback. The new "Runtime" : "nodejs4.3" is now used while creating or
updating these functions.

condor_annex version 0.0.3

Provided delete-failed-stacks.sh. This bash script is intended to be run
periodically by cron to remove AWS CloudFormation Stacks that have a
DELETE_FAILED StackStatus, which are created occasionally when
condor_annex hits a known race condition during annex shutdown.

condor_annex version 0.0.2

Changed URL for S3 bucket that stores CloudFormation template and
launch-configuration files. Also commented out yum update -y
aws-cfn-bootstrap in launch-configuration UserData.

condor_annex version 0.0.1

Commented out call to the subroutine waitForNodesInPool in the main
condor_annex script. This subroutine does not account for the existence
of other HTCondor pools and the potential flocking of jobs between them,
where the annex instances may be connected to another central manager.
It assumes COLLECTOR_HOST on the localhost executing condor_annex is
the annex central manager. In the future, waitForNodesInPool should be
modified to use the condor_status -pool option to explicitly query the
correct COLLECTOR_HOST. However, any such modification should also
attempt to take into account whether or not the COLLECTOR_HOST may be
different depending on which daemon is trying to contact the central
manager. For example, this may occur when the annex instances contact
the central manager via a private IP address, while the submit node
contacts it via a public IP address.

condor_annex version 0.0.0

A more "stable" fork of the main condor_annex project available at
https://github.com/htcondor/htcondor.git -b V8_5-condor_annex-branch.
This version of condor_annex is intented for my own development and
testing purposes only.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.8

Updated all gnuplot figures again to utilize the output generated
by the new default simulation in the gpecn1Dtdpbc.sh run script.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.7

Updated all copyright notices.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.6

Updated Makefile to support a multiple compiler configuration modeled
after the gpse (https://github.com/mkandes/gpse) Makefile. Again, this
change was made to help investigate potential compiler and performance
tuning optimizations moving forward.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.5

Increased the spatial resolution of the default simulation in the
gpecn1Dtdpbc.sh run script by approximately 5x. This change was made
simply to increase the computational problem size to help investigate
potential compiler and performance tuning optimizations moving forward.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.4

Updated all gnuplot figures to utilize the output generated by the
default simulation of the gpecn1Dtdpbc.sh run script.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.3

Converted README to README.md. Reset default simulation of the
gpecn1Dtdpbc.sh run script to be one of the example simulations that
exhibits 'An Initial Angular Momentum Dependence of the Sagnac Effect
for Matter Waves'. Also updated CHANGELOG and removed legacy TESTED
sections in the header of the Makefile.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.2

Added wave_function_switch=2, which allows wavefunc.x to generate a pair
of Bogoliubov-like plane wave excitations on top of a constant
background ground-state solution for a one-dimensional ring.

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.1

minor modifications to the run script gpecn1Dtdpbc.sh; added helper
script gs-convert-eps-to-png.sh to convert eps files generated by
freqtime.gpi and spacetime.gpi to png files; also created TRANSFORM
program to study how Doppler effect may impact Sagnac phase shift
simulations

GPECN1DTDPBC version 0.5.0

A rebuild of GPECN1DTDPBC from M. C. Kandes, "Sagnac Interferometry with
Bose-Einstein Condensates in a Uniformly Rotating Ring Trap", Ph.D.
Qualifying Exam, Claremont Graduate University & San Diego State,
University (2011).
